title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
subtitle: earthy, silky, deeply savoury
excerpt: A mix of fresh chestnut mushrooms and a small amount of dried mushrooms gives this soup a deep flavour. The dried mushrooms add an intensity that fresh alone cannot achieve. Blended smooth with cream, it is rich enough to serve as a starter or a light main.
sourceNotes: Cream of mushroom soup is a European classic with roots in French and British cooking. The addition of dried mushrooms is a common Italian and Eastern European technique for deepening flavour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding cream. Stir in cream after reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

content.text: Soak the dried mushrooms first. Their soaking liquid is packed with flavour -- pour it into the soup carefully, leaving any grit behind at the bottom of the bowl.

items.prepNote: soaked in 200ml hot water for 20 minutes

content.text: Soak the dried mushrooms in 200ml hot water for 20 minutes. Drain and squeeze, keeping the soaking liquid. Chop the soaked mushrooms roughly.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the fresh mushrooms in two batches. Cook without stirring for 3 minutes each batch until golden. Remove and set aside.
Lower the heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and thyme. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return the mushrooms to the pan. Add the stock, the soaked mushrooms, and the strained soaking liquid. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the thyme stalks. Blend until smooth. Stir in the cream.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

items.cause: Mushrooms were steamed rather than browned
items.fix: Cook mushrooms in batches over high heat so they colour rather than steam.

items.cause: Soaking liquid was poured in carelessly
items.fix: Let the soaking liquid settle and pour it off slowly, leaving the last tablespoon behind.

content.text: Cream of mushroom soup is found across Europe, from French bisques to British cream soups to Eastern European forest mushroom soups. The technique of combining fresh and dried mushrooms comes from Italian and Polish cooking, where dried porcini are used to build deep flavour in simple broths. This version blends both traditions.
